title: In 1902, a Volcano Erased a City in Under a Minute. A Prisoner Survived

scenes.text: In 1902, a volcano erased a whole city in under a minute.
scenes.keywords: volcano eruption pyroclastic flow ash cloud

scenes.text: Mount Pelee, Martinique. At eight in the morning, the mountainside burst open.
A glowing cloud of gas and ash raced down at over 100 miles an hour, hotter than 1,000 degrees.
It reached Saint-Pierre in two minutes. 28,000 people died.
Inside the city, two people lived. One was a prisoner, locked in a stone cell with one tiny window.
He joined the circus. The man who survived a volcano.

description:
On 8 May 1902, Mount Pelee on Martinique erupted and a pyroclastic flow destroyed the city of Saint-Pierre in moments.
The cloud of gas and ash moved at over 100 miles an hour and killed about 28,000 people. Inside the city only two people survived, one of them a prisoner named Ludger Sylbaris, protected by the thick walls of his cell. He later toured with the Barnum and Bailey circus.
Would you rather be locked in a cell that day, or on a ship in the harbour? Comment below.
first_comment: The prisoner, Ludger Sylbaris, was pardoned after the eruption and toured America with the circus as the only man to survive a volcano. Would you have stayed in the city when the mountain started smoking?
